title: Check yourself: Reviewing a proposal, and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A proposal has a forbidden call in its code and a description of a single line. What does the gate decide, and what does the report list?

options.text: A revision request, with the short text as the first problem the gate meets
options.says: Ruled out because a refusal comes first: "A refusal comes before a revision, because a fix cannot make a forbidden call acceptable and a revision would invite the agent to try."

options.text: A refusal, with the weakness of the text still noted beside it
options.says: A refusal wins and the findings stay in the report.

options.text: An approval behind a gate, with the forbidden call to be removed later in the run
options.says: Ruled out because the refusal stands: "A proposal with a refusal is refused, whatever else is true of it."

options.text: A refusal, with the findings dropped from the report
options.says: Ruled out because the findings are kept: "The report keeps the findings of a refused proposal, so the agent, and the log, can see everything that was wrong and not only the first thing."

questions.stem: A policy allows a timeout of at most 10 seconds, and a proposal asks for exactly 10. What does the gate do?

options.text: Flags it, since a limit should leave some room below it for safety
options.says: Ruled out because the margin is not the gate's to add: "the margin belongs in the number that the policy sets".

options.text: Flags it, since only a request below the limit counts as safe to run
options.says: Ruled out because the value is allowed: "A limit is a number that the policy allows, so a value equal to the limit is allowed."

options.text: Accepts the figure, since a request that reaches the ceiling has not passed it
Accepts it, since a person will sign the proposal off afterwards
options.says: Ruled out because a timeout within the limit needs no person: "The timeout may equal its limit and the memory may equal its limit, and one second or one megabyte more is flagged."

questions.stem: A reviewer approved a tool last week. Today the agent submits a changed version with an added write. What happens?

options.text: It goes through the gate again as a new proposal
options.says: A changed tool is a new proposal.

options.text: It runs behind a gate if the old version had been gated as well
options.says: Ruled out because the earlier gating does not carry over: "the person approved what they read and not what the agent might write next".

options.text: It runs, with the approval covering every version of that tool
options.says: Ruled out because the approval is not blanket: "An approval belongs to one proposal."

options.text: It is refused, with a tool allowed to be approved once and never changed
options.says: Ruled out because a changed tool is not forbidden, only reviewed again: "A changed tool is a new proposal and goes through the gate again".
